CHAPTER I

The cottage at the end of the lane belonged to Elizabeth Harding, and she had lived there for eleven years.

"I will not sell it," she said.

Mr. Darcy Colman, who had come from the city with a folder of papers, looked up from the table. "The offer is generous," he replied.

"It is not generous," Elizabeth said. "It is merely large."

Colman smiled at that. Darcy had heard the phrase before, from other people, and he had never liked it.

Elizabeth walked to the window. The orchard was grey with rain.

"You have not seen the orchard," she said.

"I have seen the plans," Darcy replied.

CHAPTER II

By noon the rain had stopped, and Elizabeth took the path behind the cottage.

Darcy followed at a distance. He had not been invited.

"You are persistent," she said.

"I am employed," Darcy said. "There is a difference."

Elizabeth laughed, and the sound carried further than she intended.
